emma-sales: Hey team — Acme POC hitting 401 on /v1/generate. They say same key works in Postman but our app gets 401. Customer: acme-dev@acme.com. Can someone look?

alex-se: Do we have request headers and the curl from the app? Postman sometimes auto-adds extra headers.

emma-sales: curl they sent: `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk.dev_ABC123\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{\"input\":\"hi\"}'` — response 401 with body `{\"error\":\"invalid_org_claim\"}`.

raj-eng: That error indicates the key is org-bound but the request is missing the org header. For private DPs we require `X-Redwood-Org` or `X-Project-Id` depending on binding. Ask them to dump headers.

maya-support: Pulling logs for dev key sk.dev_ABC123... I see `auth.check: token_kind=scoped_key, bound_to=project:proj_6789, claims_missing: org`. So the key is bound to a project, not the org. If the app sends `X-Org: org_000` it will 403.

alex-se: Two common mistakes: 1) Using a project-scoped key while app sets org header; 2) Using a demo key that isn't valid in the customer's tenant. Confirm which environment the app points at (hosted vs dedicated).

emma-sales: The app is pointing to their dedicated endpoint `https://eu-1.acme.redwood.private/v1/generate` (they're on Dedicated).

raj-eng: Ah — dedicated endpoints enforce tenant binding differently. For dedicated, keys issued from the control plane are tenant-bound; the request should set `X-Project-Id: proj_6789` and NOT set `X-Redwood-Org`. Also ensure the Authorization header is only `Bearer <key>` and there are no stray `Authorization: Basic` being added by a proxy.

maya-support: Quick repro steps to send to customer:
```
curl -v \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk.dev_ABC123\" \
  -H \"X-Project-Id: proj_6789\" \
  https://eu-1.acme.redwood.private/v1/generate -d '{\"input\":\"hello\"}'
```
If that returns 200 we're good. If 401 persists, ask them to attach the `x-rw-trace` id from the 401 response.

emma-sales: Sent instructions. They replied: `still 401, trace=trace_202303`. Attached app logs showing missing X-Project-Id header.

raj-eng: Looks like the app runtime strips custom headers (common in some JS frameworks or when proxying). Ask them to check the client/framework and any intermediate proxies (NGINX/Envoy) for header_whitelist rules.

alex-se: Also confirm the key's allowed_scopes include `generate` — if they used an embeddings-only key you'd get a permissions 403 not 401, but worth double-checking: `key.scopes = [\"embeddings\"]` would fail for /generate.

maya-support: I rotated a temporary test key bound to their project and sent it privately to Emma. She confirmed test key returned 200 from their app.

emma-sales: ✅ Test key works. Customer will update their proxy to forward X-Project-Id. I'll follow up with docs link to header requirements and recommend switching to a project-scoped key for dedicated POC. Thanks @maya-support @raj-eng @alex-se :rocket: 

deploy-bot: note: rotation recorded for sk.temp_987 at 1744444500

emma-sales: Closing this thread — marking POC auth issue as resolved on my side.
